Potential CME shock influences that may materialize on 12 Jul have a slight chance of increasing geomagnetic storm conditions to G1 (Minor) levels. This potential extends into 13 July, with a chance of G1 levels due to CH HSS effects and any lingering CME shock arrival influences.

A slight chance exists of an S1 Minor solar radiation storm due primarily to the mildly enhanced proton flux state and the slight risk of a solar energetic proton event from increasingly favorably located Region 3361.

There is a chance for an isolated R1/R2 - Minor/Moderate) radio blackout, and slight chance of an R3 - Strong) event 11-13 Jul, due primarily to the combined flare probabilities of mainly Regions 3366, 3361, and 3367.
There is a chance to reach G1 (Minor) storm levels 12-13 Jul should any CME-related effects be stronger than expected.
There is a slight chance of an S1 (Minor) event all three days due to the slight risk of a solar energetic proton event from ARs approaching the west limb.

Solar activity is likely to be moderate, with the continuing likelihood of M-class flares from primarily Region 3372 on 12-14 Jul. There is also a slight chance of an X-class flare (R3; Strong) event all three days.

Glancing blow CME influences may lead to active levels on 14 Jul, with a chance of G1 (Minor) storm levels. G1 levels are more likely on 15 Jul should the CME arrive as anticipated. Forecast confidence in timing and arrival of this CME are low.

There is a slight chance of a S1 (Minor) event due primarily to the slight risk of a solar energetic proton event all three days from the more favorably located Regions 3367, 3361 and increasingly favorable location of 3363.

There is a continuing likelihood of M-class flares (R1-R2; Minor-Moderate) and a slight chance of X-class (R3; Strong) events 13-14 Jul due primarily to the combined flare probabilities of Regions 3372, 3367, and 3361.

Continuing passage of the 10 Jul IMF shock and expected glancing blow arrival of the 11 Jul CME are expected to result in a chance for G1 (Minor) storm conditions on 14 Jul. Any continuing CME influences are likely to result in enough disturbances to garner G1 storm levels on 15 Jul.
There is slight chance of a S1 (Minor) storm 14-15 Jul due to the slight risk of a solar energetic proton event from the more favorably located Region 3367.

Solar activity is likely to be moderate with the likelihood of an M-class (R1-R2; Minor-Moderate) flare 14-15 Jul, with a slight decrease in activity levels to low, with a chance for an M-class flare on 16 Jul as several active regions rotate far enough beyond the limb. There is a slight chance of a X-class (R3; Strong) event all three days. The combined flare probabilities of Regions 3372, 3363, and 3367 are the primary contributors to this forecast.
G1 (Minor) geomagnetic storming is likely in intermittent periods over the course of 15 Jul in response to CME effects in combination with the onset of a negative polarity CH HSS.
There is a slight chance for a solar radiation storm (S1/Minor) through 17 Jul primarily due to the flare potential, CME history, and physical location of AR 3363.

There is a chance for M-class flares (R1-R2/Minor-Moderate radio blackouts) and a slight chance for an isolated X-class flare (R3/Strong radio blackout) through 17 Jul primarily in response to Regions 3363 and 3372.
G1 (Minor) geomagnetic storm levels are likely on 18 Jul due to CME effects.
There is a slight chance for a greater than 10 MeV proton flux event reaching the S1/Minor threshold.

Solar activity is expected to be low with a chance for M-class flares (R1-R2/Minor-Moderate radio blackouts) and a slight chance for an isolated X-class flare (R3/Strong radio blackout) through 18 Jul primarily in response to Regions 3363 and 3372.
Continuing CME influences are expected to result in unsettled to G1 (Minor) levels on 17-18 Jul with a chance for G2 (Moderate).

The greater than 10 MeV proton flux is expected to remain mildly enhanced, with a chance of S1 levels on 17 Jul due primarily to the recent activity escalation in Region 3363 and its favorable location. Proton flux is expected to continue at background on 18-19 Jul, with a slight chance of a S1 storm as Region 3363 begins to rotate to and beyond the west limb.

The combined flare probabilities of mainly Regions 3363, 3372, and 3373 have led to a forecast of solar activity likely being moderate - with C-class X-ray flux expected to continue as background levels and a likelihood of M-class flares (R1-R2; Minor-Moderate) with a chance of an X-class (R3; Strong) event on 17-18 Jul. Solar activity is expected to be low, with a chance of M-class flares and slight chance of X-class flares on 19 Jul.

Isolated periods of G1 (Minor) storm levels expected on 18 Jul due to continuing disturbances and possible arrival of a close proximity or glancing blow CME from 15 Jul. Mainly quiet to active levels are expected 19-20 Jul as CME influences wane and weak CH HSS effects remain.
There remains a slight chance for a S1 storm due mainly to the favorable location and solar energetic proton event probability from Region 3363.

There is a chance of M-class flares (R1-R2; Minor-Moderate) and a slight chance of X-class (R3; Strong) events due to the latest decreased flare and activity trends, along with the departure of Region 3363 over the next 1-2 days.

An escalation to active levels, with a likelihood of G1 storm levels on 20 Jul is forecast in reaction to any CME arrival effects. There is also a chance of G2 (Moderate) storm conditions and a slight chance of G3 (Strong) levels upon and after CME arrival. Active levels are expected on 21 Jul as any CME effects continue, with a good chance of G1 and slight chance of G2 levels. It should be noted that forecast confidence in the timing of this latest CME arrival is fair, while the intensity and duration forecast is lower confidence.

The S1 storm is expected to continue on 19 Jul and perhaps into 20 Jul. These events typically take some time to diminish below S1 levels. The source for this storm was Region 3363 and that AR rotates beyond the limb on 20 Jul, so additional events are less likely. 10 MeV proton flux is likely to drop below 10 pfu by 21 Jul, but there is a chance of the S1 event remaining in progress. Additionally, there is a chance of a re-enhancement of solar energetic protons on 20 Jul, with an anticipated CME shock arrival.

Solar activity is likely to be moderate, with a likelihood of M-class flares (R1-R2) and slight chance of an X-class (R3-Strong) event 19 Jul. A slight decrease to lower solar activity, with a chance of M-class flares and continuing slight chance of X-class flares exists on 20-21 Jul. Primary contributors to this forecast are Regions 3372, 3373, 3376 and the yet to be fully observed AR along the northeast limb. Region 3363 also contributes to this on 19 Jul, but will rotate beyond the southeast limb on 20 Jul.

Conditions on 20 Jul are likely to escalate to active conditions with periods of G1 (Minor) storm levels in response to anticipated CME shock arrival and any flanking bulk plasma influences. Forecast confidence in arrival date and timing are fair, however duration and intensity confidence is low. Should the CME be more impactful than anticipated, there is a chance of G2 (Moderate) levels and slight chance of G3 (Strong) conditions as the CME transit progresses. Any CME influences will likely continue into 21 Jul, with primarily active levels expected, but there is a chance of G1 and slight chance of G2 levels.

The greater than 10 MeV proton flux is expected to continue at S1 levels into 20 Jul with a likely return to under S1 levels later on 20 Jul. There is a chance of S1 levels to continue or occur on 21-22 Jul due to the uncertainty involved with decline in solar energetic proton prediction or potential contribution from anticipated CME arrival.

There is a chance for M-class flares (R1-R2; Minor-Moderate) and slight chance of an X-class (R3; Strong) event 20-22 Jul. Region 3363 rotates well beyond the limb on 20 Jul and the primary flare probable contributors become Regions 3372, 3373, 3376, and 3379.
